roadmapTask: Make the FeatureSync dashboard comfortable to use as an environment grows: page the version history onto its own route, give each flag its own URL, and stop a page render from reading every published version. (Items 3-5 of the user's five improvements — URL-carried filter/section state, server-side flag filtering, and sticky section nav — are planned for the next horizon.)

dimensionScores.evidence: Page 1 of total 23 / size 10 asserts exactly [23..14] and page 3 asserts [3,2,1]; the tests also assert the fetched version list equals the same exact descending array (one fetch per entry, none outside the page, never version 0), and a page-2 test asserts [13..4] to prove no repeat or skip at the boundary — the off-by-one and negative-lower-bound failure examples are each directly disproven.

clamp() guards with Number.isFinite before Math.floor/min/max, so NaN falls back to page 1 / DEFAULT_VERSION_PAGE_SIZE instead of yielding NaN keys; table tests cover page 0, -5, 1.7 and NaN all resolving to page 1 with identical entries. Above the bar: the oversized-pageSize test asserts the fetch count equals MAX_VERSION_PAGE_SIZE for a 100000 request against a 1000-version history, and the past-the-end test asserts empty entries with zero fetches, which is structural (numbers = [] when newest < 1).

BrowsePorts' member list is unchanged and no file under packages/dashboard/e2e/support/ or any fixtures file was touched; listVersionPage calls viewSnapshotVersion, never fetchSnapshotText directly. Above the bar: the test fake declares exactly readCurrentVersion and fetchSnapshotText with no cast, and its default fetch implementation is typed as BrowsePorts['fetchSnapshotText'], so a future port widening would fail typecheck in the test rather than be papered over. The one unplanned edit (const -> export const on toVersionEntry) is the minimum change satisfying this dimension's own no-duplication criterion and alters no type, signature or port.

The result carries environment, page, pageSize, totalVersions, entries, hasNewer, hasOlder; page 1 of 23 asserts hasNewer false / hasOlder true, the last page asserts hasNewer true / hasOlder false, and the three-versions-on-one-page case asserts both false. Above the bar: hasOlder is 'numbers.length > 0 && oldest > 1' rather than a length heuristic, and a dedicated test (total 20, size 10, page 2) asserts hasOlder false at an exact multiple of pageSize — the specific failure example this rubric names. totalVersions comes from readCurrentVersion, asserted as 23 even on the 3-entry last page and 0 for an unpublished environment.
